shape.text: JFrog documents an API key pattern of the leading characters AKCp followed by 69 alphanumeric characters, 73 in all.
JFrog's own client libraries recognise an API key by the leading characters AKCp8 and a length of at least 73 characters, and state no maximum length and no alphabet.
JFrog's Create API Key reference page shows a 44-character example value with base64 punctuation and no AKCp prefix, and does not say the example is representative of issued keys.
Which of the two documented forms an issued API key has, and for which Artifactory release, is not established.

unresolved.reason: JFrog states a 73-character AKCp pattern on one page and shows a 44-character unprefixed example on another, and no page ties either form to a release or says the example is schematic. A JFrog statement of the key format per release, or an issued sample under a maintainer's authority, would settle it; neither was sought.

shape.text: Whether API keys exist that begin with AKCp and a character other than 8 is not established.

unresolved.reason: The client libraries name AKCp8 while the documentation names AKCp, and no page states what the fifth character encodes. A JFrog statement would settle it.

issuance.text: A user generates an API key in the profile after unlocking it, by selecting Generate next to the API Key field; a single user has one active API key at a time.
From Artifactory 7.98 new API keys can no longer be created through the UI or the API, and the self-hosted default for the creation-blocking setting becomes true from that release.
An API key is presented in the X-JFrog-Art-API header or as the password of basic authentication with the username.

lifecycle.text: API keys were introduced in Artifactory 4.4.3, and a key generated before that release must be regenerated before it can authenticate.
API keys are saved in the database and can be retrieved through the REST API or the UI, are created without an expiry date, and by default never expire.
JFrog's API reference marks the Create API Key operation deprecated from Artifactory 7.47.x.

JFrog's API Key page states that, as notified in Artifactory 7.47.10, the API key reached End of Life at the end of Q4 2024, and a capture of the help-center page from 2025-05-20 already carries that notice.

Blocking authentication with an existing API key is a setting the administrator controls and that is off by default, both in the cloud interface from Artifactory 7.107.1 and in the self-hosted configuration.
No release or date at which authentication with an existing API key stops unconditionally is stated, and the meaning of End of Life for this feature is not defined.

unresolved.reason: The pages state deprecation, an End of Life notice, creation disabled and an optional, default-off usage block, and none names a shutdown release or date. A JFrog release note or lifecycle statement that names one, or defines End of Life, would settle it.

collisions.text: JFrog says reference tokens can be used like API keys, in the X-JFrog-Art-Api header or as basic-authentication credentials, so a value in those positions can be an API key or a reference token.

JFrog's comparison page gives two patterns side by side: reference tokens begin cmVmd followed by 59 alphanumeric characters, and API keys begin AKCp followed by 69, and a capture of that page from 2025-10-08 already states both.

openQuestions.text: The calendar dates of Artifactory 4.4.3, 7.47.10, 7.84.x, 7.98 and 7.107.1, and whether the cloud platform applied the changes on the same dates as self-hosted releases, are not established.

unresolved.reason: The pages date the lifecycle by Artifactory release and quarter only. JFrog release notes would settle it.
